stories.title: Microsoft has a new machine learning tool to improve weather forecasts
stories.summary: Old-school physics-based weather forecasting and even new AI models typically become less reliable beyond two weeks, a problem Microsoft claims to have solved using machine learning. Researchers with the company say they’ve found a new, cost-effective way to make more accurate weather forecasts two to six weeks in advance — allowing farmers and emergency responders to plan ahead with greater certainty. The findings were published today in the journal Nature, and the tool is now open-source software. Microsoft joins Google, Nvidia, and other companies developing AI tools for weather forecasting. Instead of creating a new standalone weather model, Microsoft’s latest research in this realm uses machine learning to correct bias in existing models.

stories.title: NASA’s Chandra Breaks Down ‘Treble Clef’s’ Galaxy Cluster Collision
stories.summary: Astronomers have used NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory to break down the cause of a remarkable formation of radio waves they have nicknamed the “Treble Clef” because its distinct shape strongly resembles the musical symbol. The researchers discovered the Treble Clef is likely caused by an outburst from a supermassive black hole, followed by a collision of two galaxy clusters. A paper describing the findings, led by Andrea Botteon of the National Institute for Astrophysics, or INAF, in Italy, published Wednesday in the Astronomy & Astrophysics journal.

stories.title: Starlink restrictions in Ukraine war linked to political situation, Zelensky aide says
stories.summary: New restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine's weapons can travel and stay connected to the Starlink internet network have disrupted Ukraine's battlefield "missions", President Volodymyr Zelensky's adviser has warned. Serhiy Beskrestnov said Ukraine had not been told about speed limits set overnight at 100mph (160km/h) by Elon Musk's SpaceX company. Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to effectively guide drones to Russian targets and also protect Ukrainian skies. Beskrestnov said SpaceX's move "cannot be a coincidence and is related to the current political situation". The firm has not commented.

stories.title: More students are ruling out colleges based on politics, poll finds
stories.summary: This audio is auto-generated. Please let us know if you have feedback. The share of students who say they have ruled out colleges solely because of a state’s politics has jumped 10 percentage points in just three years, according to a poll released Tuesday from the higher education consultancy Art & Science Group. That share came to 34% in summer 2026. The spike since 2023 represents “a consistent and legitimate upward trend” rather than “simply a one-time reaction to a particular political moment,” according to the Art & Science Group’s report on the poll’s findings.

stories.title: 'It's rough out here': Americans struggle with rising inflation
stories.summary: Image source, Kathryn Vaughn Image caption, Kathryn Vaughn works many odd jobs to supplement her teacher's salary ByAna Faguy Kathryn Vaughn returned to work at a rural West Tennessee elementary school this autumn with a lot more stress on her plate than in previous years. The 46-year-old, like many Americans, is juggling how to provide for her family with rising costs of, as she described it, "everything". She spends her days working three different jobs to support her family of four, including as a primary school art teacher, as US inflation continues to rise. Inflation in September was above forecasts.
stories.displayTitle: 'It's rough out here': Americans struggle with rising inflation
stories.originalSummary: US inflation continues to rise, and this month the jump was above forecasts. Here's how some are surviving.
stories.dateEvidence: Over the past 12 months, prices rose by 3.7% - up from 3.4% in the 12 months to August, according to officials numbers released on Wednesday.

stories.title: Cornell bans all fraternity parties over gang sex assault allegations
stories.summary: Cornell bans all fraternity parties over gang sex assault allegations Image source, Getty Images Image caption, State officials and others have criticised how Cornell and local prosecutors handled the case ByMadeline Halpert Updated 6 hours ago Cornell University is banning all parties at fraternity houses as it faces a backlash over its handling of an alleged sexual assault on campus two years ago. Last month, a woman known as Jane Doe filed a lawsuit alleging she was plied with drugs and raped by several men in 2024 at a party at a Cornell fraternity house.
stories.displayTitle: Cornell bans all fraternity parties over gang sex assault allegations
stories.originalSummary: The school has faced an uproar over how it handled assault allegations brought by a woman known as Jane Doe.
stories.dateEvidence: In a statement on Tuesday, Cornell's president, Michael Kotlikoff, announced a series of measures responding to the alleged assault, including the end to fraternity parties for the remainder of the university year.
